step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates HBO Max's automated security detection and remediation framework. On the left ('Detection'), security signals are gathered via CloudTrail (real-time infrastructure events), GuardDuty (anomaly detection from DNS, VPC flow, and CloudTrail logs), Inspector, and AWS Config. Inspector and AWS Config pass findings into Security Hub, which aggregates them and routes alerts to EventBridge alongside direct events from CloudTrail and GuardDuty. EventBridge acts as the central router between Detection and Remediation. On the right ('Remediation'), EventBridge triggers Lambda functions, which execute auto-remediation (deleting or fixing misconfigured resources). These custom security Lambdas are defined and deployed using Cloud Custodian YAML rules. Once remediation occurs, Lambda notifies security engineers via Slack and updates Security Hub with the status and timestamp.

nodes.notes: Notification channel where Lambda sends remediation activity alerts.

edges.notes: CloudTrail funnels real-time infrastructure events into EventBridge.
EventBridge triggers Lambda functions to remediate misconfigurations.
Lambda posts remediation activity messages into Slack.
Lambda updates Security Hub with remediation timestamp and resolution status.
GuardDuty triggers EventBridge events upon detecting malicious activity or anomalies.
Inspector routes vulnerability findings directly into Security Hub.
AWS Config security rule evaluations feed into Security Hub.
Security Hub routes aggregated detection events into EventBridge for automated remediation.
Cloud Custodian YAML policies generate and deploy remediation Lambdas.
